The North Chicago-based biopharmaceutical company posted brisk double-digit revenue growth, powered by the accelerating performance of its next-generation immunology assets Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which together have more than replaced the revenue lost from biosimilar competition to its former blockbuster anti-inflammatory therapy. The results arrive as the broader market navigates a cautious stretch ahead of pivotal technology and retail earnings, Federal Reserve minutes, and the approach of the Thanksgiving holiday. The guidance raise represents the latest in a series of upward revisions that have characterized AbbVie's trajectory throughout the year, reflecting both the breadth of its commercial execution and the growing confidence in the durability of its immunology franchise transition. Skyrizi, an interleukin inhibitor approved for psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, posted brisk sales growth that reflected both deepening market penetration in existing indications and the expanding use of the therapy in newly approved settings. Rinvoq, a JAK inhibitor with a broad label spanning rheumatoid arthritis, atopic dermatitis, ulcerative colitis, and other inflammatory conditions, likewise delivered robust growth as physician adoption continued to accelerate. Together, Skyrizi and Rinvoq have crossed a critical inflection point where their combined revenue now exceeds the peak-year sales that Humira generated before biosimilar entry. This milestone represents a remarkable commercial achievement and validates the company's multi-year strategy of dedicating resources to next-generation immunology assets designed to address a broad spectrum of autoimmune and inflammatory conditions with improved efficacy and differentiated mechanisms of action. While Humira revenue continued to decline during the quarter as biosimilar competitors captured market share, the pace of erosion has begun to stabilize, indicating that the most severe phase of the competitive transition may be nearing its conclusion. AbbVie has managed the Humira transition more effectively than many observers initially anticipated, maintaining a larger residual share of the adalimumab market than the most pessimistic scenarios had projected. The stabilization of Humira erosion reflects several factors, including the stickiness of established physician-patient relationships, the robust patient support infrastructure that AbbVie has built around the product, and the complexity of biologic switching that creates natural barriers to rapid substitution. Beyond immunology, AbbVie has made meaningful strides in building out its neuroscience portfolio, with a particular focus on migraine and neuropsychiatric conditions. The company's migraine pipeline has advanced through clinical development, with recent data readouts supporting the efficacy of novel treatments targeting distinct migraine pathways. These programs complement AbbVie's existing commercial presence in neuroscience, anchored by its marketed treatments for Parkinson's disease and migraine prevention. The migraine treatment landscape has evolved significantly in recent years with the introduction of CGRP-targeting therapies that have transformed the management of both episodic and chronic migraine. AbbVie's efforts to develop next-generation migraine treatments reflect a strategic commitment to building a durable franchise in a therapeutic area characterized by large patient populations, high unmet need, and strong commercial dynamics. In the broader neuroscience space, AbbVie has advanced programs addressing conditions such as schizophrenia, depression, and Alzheimer's disease-related agitation. AbbVie's oncology segment has continued to evolve, with established franchises in hematological malignancies and emerging programs in solid tumors. The company's hematology portfolio includes marketed therapies for chronic lymphocytic leukemia and other blood cancers that have become standards of care, generating steady revenue contributions even as new competitive entrants have reshaped portions of the treatment landscape. The company has also directed resources toward next-generation oncology approaches, including antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted small molecules that aim to extend its oncology reach into solid tumor settings where the unmet medical need remains substantial. These pipeline commitments reflect AbbVie's recognition that oncology represents one of the largest and fastest-growing therapeutic markets globally, and that a credible presence in this space is essential for a diversified biopharmaceutical company. Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision. Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings. We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements. content: AbbVie, Gilead, and Becton, Dickinson have all beaten the S&P 500 this year. Two are Dividend Kings, and Gilead has raised its payout by 74.5% over the past decade. Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks continue dominating headlines on Wall Street. That probably won't change anytime soon. But investors shouldn't be so distracted by the AI revolution that they forget there are attractive investment opportunities elsewhere. Consider the following three healthcare dividend stocks: AbbVie(NYSE:ABBV), Gilead Sciences(NASDAQ:GILD), and Becton, Dickinson(NYSE:BDX). All three have crushed broader equities this year, and they still have plenty of upside ahead for investors willing to stay the course. Read on to find out more. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again.In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » AbbVie did not perform well in the first four months of the year, but it has recovered, and its shares are now up 29% to date, while the S&P 500 has gained 10%. There are several reasons behind the drugmaker's strong performance, perhaps none more important than its two biggest growth drivers, Skyrizi and Rinvoq. These two immunology medicines are performing better than management -- and Wall Street -- expected. Considering they won't lose patent protection anytime soon, and AbbVie will face no other major loss of patent exclusivity through the end of this decade, we can expect consistent revenue and earnings growth over the medium term. Still, Skyrizi and Rinvoq will eventually face patent cliffs, with the former perhaps starting around 2033. The good news is AbbVie is preparing for that. AbbVie has strengthened its immunology pipeline through an acquisition and is looking to enter the fast-growing weight-loss market. Further, legacy products, especially its Botox franchise, should perform well over the long term. AbbVie's excellent underlying business will help support its dividend program. The company is a Dividend King, one of the corporations that have increased their payouts for at least 50 consecutive years. It would take something catastrophic for AbbVie to suspend or decrease its dividends. Until then, expect regular dividend increases alongside solid returns from the company. Gilead Sciences' shares have gained 37% this year on the back of improving financial results and solid clinical and regulatory progress. The biotech leader still makes most of its money from its HIV franchise, with medicines like Biktarvy doing much of the heavy lifting. And even though Veklury, a coronavirus medicine, is harming top-line growth, the company has performed well. Gilead Sciences' third-quarter product sales grew 13% year over year -- its fastest growth rate in this category in over a decade -- to $8.29 billion. Total revenue was $8.30 billion, up almost 7% compared to the year-ago period. Product sales excluding Veklury jumped 16% year over year. So, as Veklury continues to fade into insignificance, Gilead should record stronger top-line growth, especially as it has strengthened its HIV and oncology businesses this year with new approvals and important label expansions. The biotech giant's outlook appears stronger than it has been in a while, and its dividend program remains attractive. Gilead Sciences offers a forward yield of 2%, and it has increased its payouts by 74.5% over the past 10 years. Becton, Dickinson, a medical technology company, is finally bouncing back after several challenging years. Shares are up 43% to date. One reason for the company's strong performance is its excellent financial results. In the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 2026, which ended Sept. 30, Becton, Dickinson's revenue increased by 5.4% year over year to $5.3 billion. Adjusted earnings per share rose 27.3% year over year to $4.15. That's a strong performance for the healthcare giant. Another factor behind Becton, Dickinson's results is that it is benefiting from the soaring demand for GLP-1 products and should continue to do so over the medium term. Growing demand for injectable diabetes and weight-loss medicines is driving significant increases in sales of prefillable syringes and self-injection devices for GLP-1 drugs. With the GLP-1 market projected to expand rapidly over the next five to 10 years, this tailwind may be just starting for Becton, Dickinson. Meanwhile, the company's underlying business outside of that is resilient and highly predictable. Becton, Dickinson generates most of its revenue from recurring consumables. Finally, Becton, Dickinson is an excellent dividend stock. It is also a Dividend King with a streak of 55 consecutive payout increases.
